title: Pins as strategy: asking the question

D0.outcome: Explains that a pin can shape a whole game and that a pin is sometimes tolerated.

D1.outcome: Given a bishop pin on a knight, lists the four policies (put the question, ignore, bring up reserves, hold the choice) and says which suits the structure.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled opening positions, decides whether to ask the bishop (with a flank pawn push) by checking whether the centre can open.

D3.outcome: Predicts how a changed centre structure turns a good question into a weakening move.

misconceptions: The question always wins a tempo.
conditions: The question is good when the driven bishop lands on a desert that cannot be brought to life because the centre cannot be opened.
It is bad when the centre can open or the pawn advance leaves the king exposed to a break.
contrasts: The centre can open, so the bishop revives.
The question is disorganising for the side that asks it, so it needs compensation.
